claims.text: Setting the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
Both Terraform and OpenTofu can use Pulumi Cloud as a state backend (documented at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/).
The page /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ exists (the Pulumi Cloud Terraform state backend guide).
`PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is an environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service that specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API, for example `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`.
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
The DNS record for the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` domain should point at the same host that serves `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` in a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud deployment.
Setting `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN` is supported in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud; a separate domain is not required for the Terraform-compatible API.

The Pulumi Cloud Terraform state backend guide uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login` / `tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.

For a self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, Terraform/OpenTofu users should substitute the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value for `tf.pulumi.com` in the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
